accuracy.evidence: Matches NC 2013 Year 1 Number and place value ('read and write numbers from 1 to 20 in numerals and words'). Every word and spelling checked against the dictionary forms: thirteen, fifteen, eighteen (one t), eleven, twelve, twenty; -ty words thirty 30, fifty 50, eighty 80, seventy 70. Teen sums checked: seventeen 17, fourteen 14, nineteen 19 as 1 ten and 7, 4, 9 ones; robot 61 for sixteen and 20 for twelve are wrong, 14 and 20 right. The sorter calls 13-19 teen numbers explicitly, and m9 asks which word does not end in -teen, so the 11/12 naming question is avoided. Parameterised 10+a stays 11 to 19 at every corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented teen-word errors (Fuson 1988; Miura 1987 on irregular English teen words): ones written first (teen scene 71 feedback, robot sixteen 61, p3, m3, m6, challenge 'order'), -teen versus -ty (70 key feedback, spelling distractors thirty/fifty/eighty, challenge 'ty'), invented spellings threeteen, fiveteen, eightteen and twoteen (spell scene, p4, p5, m4, m8, challenge 'thir', 'fif', 'own'), twelve/twenty confusion (track and robot), and reading from the first letter only, six versus seven (read scene feedback, m5, challenge 'first').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagnumword is about the written form of number words: a word card read to a numeral key, a tens box and ones box that refuses 71 with the say-order explanation, spelling choices built from the real thir/fif/eigh/own slips, word cards dragged onto an 11-20 track, and a robot transcribing heard words. No other flagship lab works on number words; it differs from flagbundle and flagtenten (bundling tens with objects) and flagcmpnum (comparing numerals). The lab_distinct gate measures it under 30% against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers the order rule by building: typing 7 then 1 for seventeen gives feedback that 7 is the ones, and the correct build lights one full ten frame plus 7 dots. In the read scene a wrong numeral that shares the first letter is named ('six and seven both start with s'). The track scene places eleven, twelve and twenty, showing they have no teen. Done messages state each rule only after the task.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'Yes, the first letter is enough' (seven is offered as a key and is refused for six), '7, because you say seven first' (the tens box rejects 71 for seventeen), and 'fiveteen: five + teen' (the spelling scene refuses fiveteen and explains five changes to fif).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions; every wrong option carries a slip tag with its own message: order (ones written first), ty (-ty means tens), fif, thir, own (11 and 12 have their own words), first (same first letter) and teen (a -teen word is more than ten). In the lab, wrong taps also name the slip, for example 'sixteen says six first, but six is the ones' and 'Twelve and twenty both start with tw'.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and one idea each (numeral versus number word, teen order, spelling changes, eleven/twelve/-ty); validate_lessons readability passes for kid and adult text. Lab banners are short, e.g. 'Build the numeral for: seventeen' and 'Drag each card to its numeral'. Curriculum words numeral, digit, tens and ones are defined in the first kid sentence.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid sentence gives a rule, an example or a warning; the adult text gives Year 1 placement and key words, the 71 mistake with a ten-frame fix, the predictable spelling slips, and what each lab scene does. The content gate finds no filler phrases and the explanation is under 12% similar to any other lesson.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px phone screenshots in light and dark for every scene before and after Show me: number keys are a 2 x 5 grid of about 60 px tiles, the 11-20 track wraps to two rows of five 60 px boxes with the placed word inside the box, word cards are 2 x 2 tiles about 150 px wide, and banners fit on one line. Every scene also has large labelled buttons under the canvas (56 px young-lab buttons).

accessibility.evidence: Everything on the canvas has a labelled button twin: numerals 1-10, digits 0-9, each spelling, Pick the card eleven then Put eleven on 11, Right and Slip. The canvas aria-label is updated with every message, the challenge feedback is a polite live region, the walk gate's axe run is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, and a 360 px check found no lesson control under 44 x 44 px.
